author: Reuters
description:
The US ⁠is seeking answers from Nvidia on ⁠its chip sales to China and will find out who was in charge of compliance at the company formerly led by Jensen Huang, who resigned following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, US Treasury Secretary ‌Scott Bessent said on Sunday.
“We’ve been in touch with the temporary management, with the lead directors, with their lawyers, and we do need answers … It behoves Nvidia to move quickly on this because we want to know what the culture was,” Bessent...
title: US seeks answers on Nvidia’s sale of chips to China, Bessent says

author: Victoria Bela
description:
A US-based mathematician has stunned the community by claiming to have solved the nearly 170-year-old Riemann hypothesis using artificial intelligence (AI).
The news broke on Friday as a major conference opened in southern China’s Shenzhen, where world-leading mathematicians have gathered until Monday to mark the 200th anniversary of the birth of Bernhard Riemann – the German pioneer behind one of the field’s greatest unsolved problems.
The claim sent shock waves through the mathematics...
title: Has AI solved the Riemann hypothesis? Claim makes waves at 200th birthday event in China

author: Chao Kong
description:
Photographs showing weathered and peeling radar-absorbing coatings on the US Air Force’s F-22 Raptor have repeatedly raised concerns in recent years.
China faces similar engineering challenges with its J-20 stealth fighter. Photographs circulating online have also been presented as evidence of how surface damage could compromise the stealth fighter’s ability to evade radar detection.
But no one tells the public exactly how.
Now, laboratory measurements by Chinese scientists suggest that losing...
title: Chinese J-20’s radar signature could nearly double with 10% stealth coating loss: study

author: Carol Yang
description:
Xie Jun, a deputy general manager of state energy giant China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC), is under investigation for suspected corruption, China’s top anti-graft watchdog announced on Sunday.
The Communist Party’s Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI) said in a brief online statement that Xie was “currently undergoing disciplinary review and supervisory investigation” by the CCDI and the National Supervisory Commission for suspected “serious violations of discipline and law”, a...
title: China’s shale gas star Xie Jun under investigation for corruption: authorities

author: Zhao Long
description: When Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen on November 19, the images were historic. The three leaders issued a four-point declaration towards peace, addressing UN reform, energy security, concerns over abuses of jurisdiction by the International Criminal Court, and nuclear risk reduction. Yet the meeting produced considerably less than a grand bargain on substantive geopolitical or security issues. As a result, some media...
title: No grand bargain at Xi-Trump-Putin meeting? That was never the point

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Small multirotor and first-person view drones are now widely used – and one of the most challenging new threats – on the modern battlefield.
These drones are small, they fly at low altitudes usually off the traditional air defence radars, and combined with their manoeuvrability they are difficult to detect. A camera on an FPV drone gives the operator a live video feed that can be viewed through goggles, a headset or screen.
These drones can be used for precision strikes against personnel,...
title: How is the PLA countering small FPV drones and their swarms?

author: Orange Wang
description:
China has narrowed its power gap with the US in Asia to a record low, largely due to Washington’s own “missteps”, according to an Australian think tank’s annual gauge.
The 2026 edition of the Lowy Institute’s Asia Power Index, released on Sunday, painted a picture of an “increasingly contested regional balance of power”.
While the US remains the most powerful nation in the region, its comprehensive power score fell for a second straight year to 78.9 out of 100, and its lead over second-placed...
title: Washington’s ‘missteps’ narrow US lead over China in annual Asia power ranking

author: Caroline Lin
description:
Beijing has signalled its readiness to maintain close ties with Serbia’s new government, as the victorious Student List prepares to take power and scrutinise major public projects, including those involving Chinese firms.
The message was delivered by Li Ming, China’s ambassador to the country, in an interview published last weekend by the Belgrade-based newspaper Politika.
The two nations were “ironclad friends”, Li said, stressing that China had always approached its relations with Serbia from...
title: Despite Serbia’s political earthquake, China hopes ties will stay rock solid

author: Albee Zhang
description:
China and Vietnam completed their latest joint naval patrol in the Gulf of Tonkin on Saturday, according to the official newspaper of the People’s Liberation Army.
The two-day exercise, which included formation manoeuvres, comes as the neighbours work to strengthen maritime security cooperation despite rival territorial claims in the South China Sea.
Spanning 32 hours and 351 nautical miles (650km), the routine patrol came on the heels of historic trilateral talks between the leaders of China,...
title: PLA anti-submarine ships conduct South China Sea patrol with Vietnamese navy

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Beijing has called for the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to rescind its ban on Chinese telecoms operators directly accessing US phone numbers, vowing to take measures to safeguard its own interests.
On Thursday, the US agency voted to adopt a proposal barring Chinese telecoms operators – including China Mobile, China Telecom and China Unicom – from directly accessing US phone numbers, citing national security grounds.
On Sunday, China’s Ministry of Commerce said in a statement that...
title: Beijing vows to defend interests as US bars Chinese telecoms from accessing phone numbers

author: Wei Wei
description:
In his keynote speech at the Apec CEO Summit in Shenzhen on November 18, President Xi Jinping quoted the ancient Chinese saying “fan yi zhi dao yu shi jie xing”, which suggests that all approaches must move with the times to be of benefit.
Of all the messages in his speech, the eight characters of the Chinese saying caught my attention. Rooted in the I Ching, or Book of Changes, the phrase carries a simple but important idea: progress comes from creating benefits while recognising that the ways...
title: Xi’s Apec summit speech is a call to cooperation suited to the times

author: Laura Zhou
description:
A rival joint bid by Belgium and Chile to host the secretariat for the landmark UN high seas treaty could present a fresh diplomatic test for Beijing ahead of the 2027 vote.
Observers say the surprise November 6 announcement of their merged bid to oversee the Agreement on Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) will complicate China’s efforts to secure its first major UN body headquarters.
The agreement, which took effect in January, is the first legally binding framework to protect...
title: How the battle to host UN high seas treaty tests China’s push for global leadership

author: Holly Chik
description:
A 2022 study exploring a vaccine design for pan-Sars-CoV-2 immunity was retracted last month after its lead author, then in Britain, admitted to fabricating data and falsifying images in the paper.
While the retraction of the study, widely cited up until this year by international scientists, marks a significant blow to vaccine research, virologists said the foundational science targeting broader coronavirus immunity remained robust and independent of the retracted study.
Citation records show...
title: How a retracted UK Covid-19 vaccine study tainted the global hunt for mutation-proof shots
